records.title: Neurological altitude decompression sickness among U-2 pilots: 2002–2009
records.locator: Printed pp. 675–677, Human and Medical Factors, Tables I–II, and Figure 2

table_reconciliation.note: MP7 and AP4 each have two printed rows. The Table I footnote identifies three additional confirmed events without row-level exposure details. Table II's footnote groups multiple incidents and/or symptoms without assigning another incident count.

diagnostic_wording.abstract: The abstract calls four incidents possible.
diagnostic_wording.results: Results and Table I call the four incidents probable.
diagnostic_wording.treatment_text: Page 677 calls all 20 cases confirmed while reporting 19 appropriate treatments. The Results identify 16 confirmed and four probable incidents. The treatment count has no resolved certainty denominator.
diagnostic_wording.persistent_symptoms: Page 676 describes nine of 20 pilots with lasting symptoms. The 20 described earlier are incidents, with repeated pilots. No pilot-level proportion is inferred.

case_crosswalk.basis: Jersey et al. p. 676 cite Pickard as reference 11 for a serious case with neurological and pulmonary symptoms. MP1 lists 29,200 ft physiological altitude and 10.5 hours. Pickard p. 357 reports 29,200 ft cabin altitude and more than nine hours of flight. Pickard gives neither age nor a case code. The altitude definitions are report-specific.

Jersey et al. p. 676 cite the 2010 report as reference 7 for a serious case and the MRI finding. The confirmed MP7 row matches age 47 and the nominal 28,000 ft. Table I reports BMI 32 and physiological altitude. The 2010 narrative reports BMI 31 and cabin altitude. The 2.5-hour symptom onset and 11.1-hour listed exposure duration have different meanings. No explicit ID match is printed.
